- The two quartets at 1.90 and 1.97 ppm (3H each) suggest two methyl groups
- The IR band at 1679 cm-1 is consistent with a C=O stretch

The 13C signal at 175.1 ppm is characteristic of a carboxylic acid, and the signals at 136.0 and 155.6 ppm suggest a disubstituted alkene. The two methyl groups (signals at 1.90 and 1.97 ppm in 1H-NMR, and 15.4 and 20.4 ppm in 13C-NMR) are likely attached to the alkene.

The molecular formula C8H16O2Si suggests:
- 1 trimethylsilyl group (C3H9Si)
- 1 carboxylic acid group (CO2H)
- 2 methyl groups (C2H6)
- 1 disubstituted alkene (C2H)

This points to 2,3-dimethyl-3-(trimethylsilyl)acrylic acid or a similar structure.
